html:
Antonio José de Sucre was a Venezuelan general, Bolívar's closest lieutenant, who won the decisive battles of Pichincha and Ayacucho and became president of Bolivia.

Born in Cumaná, he fought in the independence wars from his teens. He freed Quito at the Battle of Pichincha in 1822 and destroyed the last Spanish army in Peru at the Battle of Ayacucho in 1824. In 1825 the provinces of Upper Peru declared themselves independent and named their country after Simón Bolívar.

Sucre governed Bolivia from 1825 to 1828, building schools and reforming taxes, until a mutiny wounded him and he left. In 1830 he was murdered in an ambush in the mountains of southern Colombia. Bolivia's constitutional capital, the old Chuquisaca, is named Sucre in his honour.
sum: Antonio José de Sucre was a Venezuelan general, Bolívar's closest lieutenant, who won the decisive battles of Pichincha and Ayacucho and became president of Bolivia.
